Title: kSmallestPairs – Finding the K Smallest Sum Pairs

Main Goal: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2, this code finds the k pairs (one element from each array) whose sums are the smallest. It uses a custom MinHeap to efficiently generate and retrieve the next smallest sum pair in O(log k) time per operation.

How It Works:
1. MinHeap class implements a binary min-heap that stores entries of the form [sum, i, j], where sum = nums1[i] + nums2[j].
2. The kSmallestPairs function:
   – Initializes the heap with the pair (0,0).
   – Repeatedly pops the smallest-sum entry, records the corresponding pair [nums1[i], nums2[j]], and pushes two new candidates: (i, j+1) and, if j was 0, (i+1, 0).
   – Continues until k pairs are collected or the heap is empty.
This approach avoids generating all O(n·m) pairs by only exploring the next promising candidates.

Title: Heap Sort in Ascending Order

Main Goal:
This code implements the heap sort algorithm by building a min-heap from the input array and then repeatedly extracting the smallest element to produce a sorted array in ascending order.

Functions:
1. heapAscending(nums):
   - Clones the input array into a heap.
   - Builds a min-heap by sifting down all non-leaf nodes.
   - Repeatedly extracts the root (smallest element), replaces it with the last heap element, reduces heap size, sifts down to restore heap order, and collects the sorted elements.
   - Returns a new array containing the input numbers sorted in ascending order.

2. siftDown(heap, i, n):
   - Restores the min-heap property for the subtree rooted at index i within the first n elements of the array.
   - At each step, compares the current node with its left and right children, swaps with the smallest child if necessary, and continues until the subtree is a valid min-heap.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Setting the Rightmost Unset Bit in an Integer

Main goal: Given an integer n, locate its least significant 0-bit (the rightmost unset bit) in its binary representation and flip it to 1, returning the new number. A helper function computes the 1-based position of the least significant set bit.

Functions:
1. getPosOfRightMostSetBit(n): Returns the 1-indexed position of n’s lowest set bit by isolating n & -n and taking log2.
2. setRightMostUnsetBit(n): 
   - If n is 0, returns 1.
   - If n has all bits set (n & (n+1) == 0), returns n unchanged.
   - Otherwise, finds the position of n’s lowest zero bit via the helper on ~n, then flips that bit in n.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: countUnsetBits Function  
Main Goal: Determine how many bit positions (from the least significant bit up through the highest bit in n) are unset (0) in the binary representation of a non-negative integer n.

Description:  
The function initializes a mask x at 1 (the lowest bit) and a counter at 0. It then loops, shifting the mask left one bit each time, until the mask exceeds n. On each iteration it uses a bitwise AND (x & n) to test whether the current bit in n is 0; if so, it increments the counter. Finally, it returns the total count of unset bits.
